newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait stock index ends week at a new record high.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait stock index ends week at a new record high.

text.p: Kuwait share index closed at 2,173.1 points on Monday, ending the trading week at a new record high ahead of a four-day holiday.
Kuwait on Tuesday marks its 1961 independence from Britain followed by Wednesday's liberation day -- Iraq's defeat in the 1991 Gulf War and its withdrawal from the small Gulf Arab state.
Trading on the Kuwait Stock Exchange resumes on Saturday.
Monday's record is 33.9 points higher from last week's close and a 19.5 point rise from Sunday.
The index is 14 percent up from the start of 1997. It rose about 40 percent in 1996.
Traders attribute the upward trend to strong year-end results by listed companies which are still being issued.

Traded value on Monday rose to 56.3 million dinars ($186.4 million) compared to last week's daily average of 51.4 million dinars. Some 190.2 million shares were traded on Monday compared with last week's daily average of 166.8 million.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest in mutual funds.
